### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f91b345ae18fcb367835fe1bdfa24f043d094992` — the merge of head `1ce77b0aaac41e3eb9e0f6187a18b35a1d8cdbcc` into base `39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f91b345ae18fcb367835fe1bdfa24f043d094992 && git checkout f91b345ae18fcb367835fe1bdfa24f043d094992
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e 1ce77b0aaac41e3eb9e0f6187a18b35a1d8cdbcc && git checkout -B drift-repro 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e && git merge --no-ff 1ce77b0aaac41e3eb9e0f6187a18b35a1d8cdbcc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39951d2a26590ff93226d3c0cf4ecfdc4136031e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **New public names — for the maintainer, approval items (not FAIL reasons):**

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts` — judged against the card's done criteria, ADR-0049 / 0141 D5 / 0143 D3 / 0146 D8, and its first consumer-to-be, `assemblePackageManifest` + the `GET /packages/:id/export` branch in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`.

- **Composition holds.** Each entry IS `PackageExportManifestSchema` (identity, pinned). `GET /packages/:id/export` answers `deps.success(manifest)`, i.e. `{ success: true, data }` with the manifest as `data`, and the route ledger's convention is "Enveloped — the named schema is the `data`". The bundle declares itself as the `data` of the same envelope, and `{ packages }` declares neither `success` nor `data`, so the client unwrap heuristic cannot misfire on it. **Holds.**
- **Done criterion "base + `.custom` pair + extending package → three installable packages".** The test fixture is exactly that triple, in dependency order, the pair carrying `overrides: { package, basedOn }` (ADR-0146 D8 item 3) and the extender carrying `objectExtensions` (the key `assemblePackageManifest` emits, `EXTENSIONS_KEY`). The shape admits it and preserves order. **Holds** at spec level; installability is the server slice's test.
- **Done criterion "nothing secret leaves" (ADR-0143 D3: `credentialRef` only).** The bundle adds no redaction rule and declares none; the docblock says the per-package export already withholds. Read in the tree, that chain is real: `assemblePackageManifest` → `protocol.getMetaItemsPerPackage` → `readFlattenedMetaItems(…, 'served', 'per-package')` → `protocol.ts:10877` `audience === 'served' ? decorateMetadataItems(…)` → `redactMetadataItem(type, item)` → the registry's `connector` redactor (`connector-credential-redaction.ts#redactConnectorItem`: withholds every `auth.*` key the instance-auth kind does not declare, every `authentication.*` key but `type`, the upstream header/env maps whole, non-object `auth` whole, URL userinfo and credential query params), the `datasource` redactor (`datasources` are not exported anyway), and `deriveCredentialRedactor` for any type whose schema marks `.meta({ credential })` (`WebhookSchema.secret` / `.headers`). `credentialRef` is a DECLARED key of every `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` variant, so it survives as the reference. The spec cannot police this structurally (the element is honestly open, ruling 4A), and it should not: one producer, one redaction, is the right rule and the docblock states it as such. **Holds.** No cleartext channel is opened by this PR; the card's credential test belongs to the server slice and is listed in its handoff.
- **Order rule (ADR-0141 D5).** `packages/core/src/hydration-order.ts#orderHydrationBatch`: dependencies first, source order where no edge decides, a cycle's members keep source order among themselves and are reported in `cycles`. The docblock's three sentences on order match that function exactly, including the cycle sentence. **Holds.** The top-level `.strict()` means a future `cycles` member on the wire is a spec change first, which the "strict" test pins (`{ ...bundle, cycles: [] }` → `unrecognized_keys`).
- **Read gate.** The docblock requires the per-package export's gate: `requireReadCapability` (`studio.access` or `setup.access`, or `isSystem`) — `packages.ts:402–430`. **Holds** as a statement of the door's rule.
- **Marker form (ADR-0049).** Declared ahead of its producer, marker in the describe, MUST-form docblock, pin test that the serving slice flips, no tracker id in customer-facing prose. Same form as the two sibling spellings on `main`. **Holds.**
- **Should-fix — the selection rule names `system` where the house names two platform scopes.** `READ_ONLY_PACKAGE_SCOPES = ['system', 'cloud']` is the one definition of "the platform's own" that the runtime reads (`isWritablePackage`, `isDisableableAppModule`). The docblock ("a package whose manifest `scope` is `system` is shipped by every runtime for itself") and the describe ("but the platform's own (manifest `scope` `system`)") encode one of the two values by hand. A `cloud`-scope package is not shipped by an open runtime either, and an "installable on the Apache-2.0 runtime" bundle has no use for it. Fix: say "a platform scope (`READ_ONLY_PACKAGE_SCOPES`: `system`, `cloud`)" in both places, or have the maintainer rule that `cloud`-scope packages ARE part of a tenant's exportable ontology (then the docblock should say why). The shape, the names and every test are unaffected either way; this is escalated under ③ item 2 for the maintainer's ruling on Q2. Not a must-fix: the rule is prose for a door nothing serves yet, the maintainer is already asked to approve it, and the server slice can carry the corrected wording with the mount.
- **Should-fix — a one-line handoff note.** The docblock could name the dispatcher-order requirement (③ item 6) beside the "never shadows" sentence, so the server slice reads both directions in the place it will read first. Cosmetic.
- **Tried to break it, and could not:** an entry with no identity is refused at `packages.N.id/name/version`; `{}` is refused at `packages`; `{ packages: [] }` parses (a deployment of platform packages only); a hand-copied open object in place of the composed element is caught only by the identity pin — which exists. The `lazySchema` Proxy is the same object `z.array(...)` holds as `.element`, so the identity pin is stable under lazy evaluation and under `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS=1`.

No must-fix. No security-relevant issue turned up (the redaction chain the docblock relies on is real in the tree and this PR opens no second path), so no security note is written.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`, judged against the ruling it implements (6568804196: a tenant exports its whole ontology to the open runtime), the ADRs it cites (ADR-0049, ADR-0141 D5, ADR-0146 D8/D11) and its first consumer (the server slice that will mount `GET /packages/export` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, reading this docblock as its order).

**What holds.** The shape `{ packages: PackageExportManifest[] }` is the right composition: one producer, no second assembly, strict at the top, open per entry as ruled for the per-package export (#12038 4A). Order, credential, gate and whole-or-absent rules each transcribe code that exists on the head (named in ①). The pin tests cover strictness, element identity, the required key, the empty bundle and the marker, and the dev's ablations show each pin is load-bearing.

**must-fix 1 — the selection rule derives "the platform's own" from `manifest.scope`, which the published spec forbids and the runtime already ruled wrong.** The describe of `packages`, the schema describe and the docblock ("a package whose manifest `scope` is `system` is shipped by every runtime for itself") all make `manifest.scope === 'system'` the predicate for what the bundle leaves out. The tree it cites says otherwise:

- `packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts:49-71` — every registry row carries `source: 'code' | 'marketplace' | 'authored'`, where `code` is "registered by the running deployment's own code: a `defineStack()` host's packages, a plugin's bundled manifest, a platform package", and "⛔ The value is the PRODUCER's statement … no reader derives it from other keys (`writable`, `manifest.scope`, a second list)". That enum is exactly "what every runtime ships for itself".
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:866-880` (#14375 / ADR-0130 Consequences row 6) — Studio once derived the same platform-versus-tenant line from `manifest.scope` alone, and the server corrected it: "a package booted from an artifact through `registerApp` is read-only whatever its scope says, and a scope-less BOOTED package lands there too".
- `ManifestSchema.scope` (`kernel/manifest.zod.ts:636`) is `.default('project')`: a plugin's bundled manifest that declares no scope is a `code` package at scope `project`.

Consequences on the card's scenario, both directions: a code package the runtime boots at the default scope is exported, and `os package install` of it on an open runtime that defines the same id is refused `409 MANIFEST_CONFLICT` ("already defined by this runtime's local code", `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1976`) — the bundle is no longer "installable packages", and the done criterion's three-package count is broken by every such entry; conversely a marketplace or authored package whose manifest carries `scope: 'system'` is dropped from the tenant's export although the target does not ship it. Meanwhile the per-package export already reads `registry.getPackage(id)`, whose row carries `source`, so the server slice has the right key in hand and nothing to derive. The fix is textual and confined to this file (plus the changeset's mirror sentence and the regenerated docs): state the rule as "every package whose registry row's `source` is not `code` (`InstalledPackageSourceSchema`) — marketplace and authored packages, a `.custom` pair among them — each once, enabled or not", and drop `manifest scope system` from the two describes and the docblock. The marker pin test can then also check that the describe names `source` and not `scope`. Until then the contract orders its first consumer to implement a predicate the spec's own ⛔ forbids. FAIL.

**should-fix 1 — the docblock pins the mount site and the ledger shape of a slice that has not been written.** "mounts `GET /packages/export` in packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, in the same change as its route-ledger row and its `PackageApiContracts` entry" names a file path and two ledger edits as this schema's contract. A route-ledger row is the house's declaration of a served route; a `PackageApiContracts` entry is not required of the lifecycle family (`package-api-assembled.zod.ts:267-312` binds the list, get, install and uninstall doors only; no route this file declares has one, and the one that did, `rollbackPackage`, was retired under #12038 3A). Keep the marker-removal rule and the ledger row; drop the `PackageApiContracts` clause and the file path so the server slice is not sent to add a binding the family does not use.

**should-fix 2 — "enabled or not" is stated without its install-side half.** The bundle exports disabled packages (status `disabled`, `PackageStatusEnum`) as installable packages, so a reinstall on the open runtime enables what the tenant had switched off, and the per-package export carries no `enabled`/status key to say so. Either carry the rule to the consumer ("the bundle does not carry the enabled state; a consumer enables every entry") in the describe, or export only enabled packages. The choice is the card's; the silence is not.
